# ui::testing::HeadlessUI

Header: `winui/testing/HeadlessUI.hpp`.

The UI host for tests, with no native window. It holds one [Window](../tree/window.md) with a [HeadlessWindowHost](headless-window-host.md) installed, laid out with a [HeadlessTextMeasurer](headless-text-measurer.md), so layout, focus, input and window-state behavior run the same on any OS with deterministic numbers.

Drive it like a real host: set content, [layout()](#layout), then feed input to [window()](#window) and advance time with [tick()](#tick). Nothing is rendered; call [Element::render()](../tree/element.md#render) with a [TestRenderer](test-renderer.md) to inspect output.

Unless a test installed its own, the window comes with a [TestClipboard](test-clipboard.md), a [TestLauncher](test-launcher.md), a [TestMessageBoxHost](test-message-box-host.md), a [TestNotifier](test-notifier.md) and a [TestJumpListHost](test-jump-list-host.md) installed ([set_clipboard()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_clipboard), [set_launcher()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_launcher), [set_message_box_host()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_message_box_host), [set_notifier()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_notifier), [set_jump_list_host()](namespace-ui-testing.md#set_jump_list_host)) for as long as this HeadlessUI lives, so a copy, a link, a message box, a notification or a jump list never reaches the OS. [clipboard()](../tree/namespace-ui.md#clipboard), [launcher()](#launcher), [message_boxes()](#message_boxes), [notifier()](#notifier) and [jump_list()](#jump_list) return them.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::testing::HeadlessUI ui = ui::testing::create_headless();
ui::Property<int> clicks{0};
ui::Control<ui::Button> save;
ui.window().set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(clicks, [](int n) { return std::to_string(n); })},
    ui::Button{.text = "Save", .on_click = [&] { ++clicks; }, .control = save},
}});
ui.layout({400, 300});

const ui::Point center = save->bounds().center();
ui::testing::seams(ui.window()).handle_pointer({center, ui::PointerButton::Left, ui::PointerAction::Down});
ui::testing::seams(ui.window()).handle_pointer({center, ui::PointerButton::Left, ui::PointerAction::Up});
REQUIRE(clicks.get() == 1);
```

## window

```cpp
Window& window()
```

The single logical window (created lazily), with a [HeadlessWindowHost](headless-window-host.md) already installed. The host owns it; the reference is valid for the lifetime of this HeadlessUI.

## host

```cpp
HeadlessWindowHost& host()
```

The fake window host (see [HeadlessWindowHost](headless-window-host.md)).

```cpp
TestClipboard* clipboard() const
```

The [TestClipboard](test-clipboard.md) this HeadlessUI installed with [window()](#window), or nullptr when a test had installed its own clipboard first.

## show

```cpp
void show(Size client, WindowState initial = WindowState::Normal)
```

Shows the window in the `initial` state, as [ui::WindowOptions::initial_state](../tree/window-options.md) does, and lays it out at `client` unless that state is Minimized.

## simulate_state

```cpp
void simulate_state(WindowState state, Size client)
```

The user changing the state from outside the app (see [HeadlessWindowHost](headless-window-host.md):: [simulate_state()](#simulate_state)), followed by the layout a real host runs at the window's new size.

## button

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<ButtonControl> button(std::string text)
```

Convenience factories. New tests should declare their tree instead, so they build through the API real callers use. `.control` gives them the same typed observers these factories return (see the class example).

Each returns a freshly owned element. Ownership transfers to whatever the caller hands it to ([StackControl::add](../layout/stack.md#add) / [Window::set_content](../tree/window.md#set_content)).

## text

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<TextControl> text(std::string text)
```

A new [TextControl](../controls/text.md#uitextcontrol) showing [`text`](#text); see [button()](#button).

## check_box

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<CheckBoxControl> check_box(std::string text, std::optional<bool> checked = false)
```

A new [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox); `checked` nullopt is the indeterminate state. See [button()](#button).


## toggle_switch

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<ToggleSwitchControl> toggle_switch(bool on = false)
```

## vertical_stack

```cpp
template <typename... Children>
std::unique_ptr<StackControl> vertical_stack(Children... children)
```

Builds a vertical stack, seeded with children in order: ui.vertical_stack(ui.text("Hello"), ui.button("Save")). Children are moved in.

## layout

```cpp
void layout(Size client)
```

Lays out the window at a client size (DIPs) using the headless measurer, as a real host does when the window is resized.

## tick

```cpp
bool tick(Duration delta)
```

Advances elapsed time by `delta` through [Window::tick()](../tree/window.md#tick). Time moves deterministically, with no real clock, for things like a [ToolTip](../controls/tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay. Returns whether the tree became dirty and needs a repaint, as [Window::tick()](../tree/window.md#tick) does.

## measurer

```cpp
const TextMeasurer& measurer() const
```

The [HeadlessTextMeasurer](headless-text-measurer.md) [layout()](#layout) uses, for measuring or laying out elements outside the window the same way.
